doc.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022

title: Recording Stanley Clarke and meeting Chick Corea
summary: Ken Scott asks Kirsh to record Clarke's trio with McLaughlin and Corea, 'Song to John'; later he is hired for Patti Smith.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Yeah it wasn’t just precision and it wasn’t just technical expertise it was using that to create beautiful communication and interplay between the guys and it was at a high level. So anyway so I enjoyed that, and so I was in that mindset and was still doing you know rock dates and then the next thing that happens is in ’74 Stanley Clarke comes in to do his recording, do an album. I think it was his second album. And so I did some assisting on that and the engineer, Ken Scott, a great engineer, said, “Listen I can’t make it tomorrow night. Why don’t you record this for me, and I’ll mix it, but if you’ll record it for me that’d be great. It’s just a trio.” And I said okay, it’s just bass, guitar and piano. And I go in and I set it up the way I thought it should be set up and in comes John McLaughlin, who I’d worked with before, and he was playing acoustic guitar, and Chick Corea comes in. So it was the three guys, and that’s when I met these characters as a group. And it was a beautiful, beautiful session. It was called “Song to John” was the name of it, a piece that Stanley had written. I think it’s in two parts. And so that was my introduction to Chick and then I didn’t see him for another I would say better part of a year. Prior to seeing him again I was interviewed to do an album for Patti Smith. She wanted to work at Electric Lady, for the vibe, you know because it was Jimi’s place and so forth. So I went and talked to her and we worked it out and I started doing the recording, and did it, and enjoyed her style. She was really a poet and that was her — I think her main impetus, I mean she enjoyed the music and so forth. That’s my view, not hers, of what she was © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
